messages:
samg: Heads-up — escalated ticket from a Dedicated customer. Calls to our API over their interface endpoint intermittently return 403 or TLS handshake failures. Public calls work fine.

maya: Do we have a repro vpc and logs? any pattern on source CIDRs or AZs?

devon: Customer says it started after they added a central NGW and some cross-account endpoint policies. They see the endpoint resolve to a public IP in some traceroutes.

alice: Can you paste the dig/traceroute and curl output? quick checks: Route53 PHZ for the service, and the VPC endpoint private dns setting. Also check endpoint policy (aws:SourceIp vs aws:SourceVpc) and SG egress rules.

samg: Paste from customer: `dig api.redwood.internal @10.0.0.2 +short` -> `34.210.11.5` (public).
traceroute shows hops leaving VPC to NAT.
curl from their app tasks: `curl -v https://api.redwood.internal/path` -> TLS alert, sometimes HTTP/1.1 403.

maya: That dig result strongly suggests split-horizon / resolver forwarding misconfig. If their resolver forwards to internet-resolving resolver, PHZ isn't being used. Are they using Route53 resolver endpoints + outbound forwarders?

devon: Also note: they use ALB in front of our service on Dedicated with TLS cert for `api.redwood.com` (public cert). If DNS resolves to public IP, SNI will match that cert but the connect path might hit a different backend and our auth JWT check sees different audience -> 403.

alice: Repro steps to ask customer: 1) from a failing task: `nslookup api.redwood.internal` and `aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=<their-vpc>` 2) `dig @<route53-resolver-ip> api.redwood.internal` 3) `openssl s_client -connect <resolved-ip>:443 -servername api.redwood.internal -quiet` include cert CN and issuer.

samg: They ran openssl s_client and pasted cert CN = `alb-backend.local` (internal cert), issuer internal CA. When we saw public IP with public cert earlier (from their ops bench), results were different. So sometimes DNS returns public IP and public cert, other times internal IP and internal cert.

maya: That smells like conditional forwarder misconfig with resolver endpoints in two regions: one forwarding to internet resolver (giving public) and one forwarding to Route53 private zone (giving private). Could be resolver rules priority or HGW/NAT path causing queries to use wrong resolver.

devon: Another possibility: they created an interface endpoint with 'enable private DNS' turned off, and then added CNAMEs in their private zone pointing to public name. That can create inconsistent name resolution depending on which resolver answers.

alice: Quick mitigation for customer: 1) ensure interface endpoint has private DNS enabled for our service name, 2) check Route53 PHZ is associated with the VPCs in question, 3) remove any CNAMEs pointing to public `api.redwood.com` in private zones, 4) check resolver rule priorities (`aws route53resolver list-resolver-rules` and `list-resolver-rule-associations`).

samg: They asked about why TLS handshake fails (not just 403). We saw: `TLSv1.2 alert handshake failure` when s_client used SNI matching public name but route landed on internal ALB that expects a different servername/ALPN. Could be ALB TLS policy rejecting unknown ALPN or backend rejecting client TLS version.

maya: Also check SGs on interface endpoint ENIs — some customers lock egress to specific ports/destinations; if egress to our public IP goes via NAT with different source IPs, some backends (our DDoS/edge) may reject because it's seen as unexpected source -> auth or rate-limit triggered.

devon: For repro I recommend we ask customer to: a) force resolution to private IP via `dig @<route53-resolver-ip> api.redwood.internal` b) `curl --resolve api.redwood.internal:443:<private-ip> https://api.redwood.internal/health -v` c) collect `tcpdump -n -i eth0 port 443` from a failing task to show dest IP and SNI.

alice: I'll draft a runbook snippet they can copy. Also flag infra to check whether our Dedicated ingress has any geo/ASN-based allowlist that might be dropping traffic from their central NGW IP range.

infra-bot: Reminder: when filing internal infra tickets include VPC endpoint ID, resolver rule IDs, PHZ ID, and sample packet captures.

samg: Customer will run the tcpdump + digs and share. I'll update thread when they respond. Thanks all :thumbsup:

maya: If they hit 403s after ensuring private DNS, we should inspect our API auth checks for `x-forwarded-for` vs client cert CN mismatch. There's a known case where ALB terminates TLS and inserts different headers that our auth logic misinterprets -> 403.

devon: Noted — if they provide a pcap, I can map source IPs and confirm if traffic hit NAT vs interface endpoint ENI.

samg: Closing interim notes: primary suspects = split-horizon DNS / resolver rule ordering / private-dns off on endpoint / endpoint policy or NGW SNAT causing source IP differences.

alice: Also add to runbook: how to check `EnableDnsHostnames` and `EnableDnsSupport` on their VPCs — missing flags can cause odd resolution behaviour for some clients.

samg: Ticket owner will share outputs. If nothing clear, we'll request short read-only access to their resolver config or run a guided debug call.
